key_points: Real activity remains solid: Fed describes solid GDP growth driven by AI capex and resilient consumption; claims at 187k are very low and unemployment ticked down to 4.2%.
June payrolls only +57k and GDPNow data is stale (1.68%), so the momentum signal is mixed rather than accelerating.
Consumer sentiment is deeply depressed (49.5) though rebounding; the oil rebound (+28% in a month) is a headwind for lower-income consumers and real growth.
Yields at 1-year highs already price resilient growth plus a hawkish Fed; from a growth lens little edge beyond slight near-term upside and mild mean reversion later.
Solid growth plus AI earnings supports equities and keeps credit spreads tight; small upward tilt for S&P 500, neutral HY spreads.
Oil's sharp spike looks supply-driven rather than demand-driven; growth softness abroad argues for slight downside over 1-3 months.
Core PCE running ~3.4% y/y with staff and participants seeing upside inflation risks and broadening price pressures; Fed dropped easing bias and a few members see a case for hikes.
June CPI fell 0.4% m/m on the post-MOU energy drop, but WTI has since rebounded 28.5% in a month to ~$92, which should feed back into headline inflation and breakevens.
10y breakevens at 2.26 (21st percentile) look low relative to the oil rebound and sticky core, giving a modest upward tilt.
Hawkish inflation backdrop into the July 29 FOMC supports front-end yields and mild bear-flattening of 2s10s; yields already at 1y highs, so edge is limited.
Rising real yields are a headwind for gold; oil after a sharp run-up carries mean-reversion risk.
Equities face inflation/rates headwind but strong earnings drift keeps probability modestly above 0.5.
Labor market is firm and edging tighter: unemployment fell to 4.2% from 4.3%, and initial claims dropped to 187k, well below the 221k of a year ago. The layoff signal is very benign.

Payroll gains have slowed to +57k in June. Still, the Fed judges job growth to be keeping pace with a slow-growing workforce, so this does not read as loosening. Wage growth of about 3.4% is not a source of inflation pressure.

A firm labor market removes the downside-employment rationale for cuts. Together with a hawkish Fed (a few participants already floating hikes), this tilts the front end modestly higher, and the 2-year should lean up more than the 10-year, a mild flattening bias.

Yields are already at the top of their 1-year range, the 2-year has risen 55bp in 3 months, and spec positioning in 2-year notes is at the 99th percentile. Much of this is priced, so the edges stay small.

A solid labor market supports earnings and consumer credit, so there is a slight lean toward equities up, HY spreads tighter and VIX lower. A stronger dollar on rate differentials is mildly favored, and gold faces a modest headwind.

Upcoming early-August and early-September jobs reports, plus the July 29 and September 16 FOMC meetings, are the key catalysts. Very low claims make an upside labor surprise somewhat more likely than a sharp deterioration.
Fed funds at 3.50-3.75% with the 2y at 4.33% means markets already price a material hiking cycle; the bar for further hawkish repricing is high.
June minutes dropped the easing bias and several members flagged hikes, but a July 29 hike is unlikely; a hawkish hold may disappoint the most aggressive pricing, slightly favoring lower 2y yields.
Yields sit at 99th 1y percentile after a +55bp 3m move in 2s; Fed's credible 'will deliver price stability' stance caps long-run breakevens and term premium drift.
Hawkish Fed relative to other central banks supports the dollar modestly; rate differentials already wide.
Equities supported by AI earnings despite higher rates; hawkish Fed tilts but does not reverse positive drift.
Oil spike re-energizes inflation risk but the Fed is expected to look through supply shocks while guarding expectations; breakevens restrained.

Early-August quarterly refunding (borrowing estimates and coupon sizing) lands inside the 1-month window; with deficits large and the Fed staff noting a shift of Treasury ownership toward price-sensitive private holders, the risk is a coupon-size increase or a hawkish forward-guidance change, which favors a higher term premium.

The term premium is already rebuilding: 10y at 4.69 is at the 99th percentile of its 1y range, and spec shorts in TY are large, so much of the supply concern is priced. That keeps the edge on higher 10y yields modest.

The Fed's reserve-management bill purchases and the low bill supply anchor the front end relative to the long end. That plus supply concentrated in coupons tilts toward 2s10s steepening, especially at 3m.
The 2y is driven by the Fed rather than by supply. TU shorts are at the 99th percentile and the 2y is near its 1y high, so there is a mild bias toward a lower 2y over 3m.
The mid-September tax date and fiscal year-end refill the TGA and drain reserves. This is a marginal tightening for liquidity, a slight headwind for risk assets and spreads, but not dominant.
Fiscal-debasement narratives offer mild support to gold despite high real yields. The dollar, oil and breakevens get little edge from the fiscal lens.
Financial conditions remain loose: NFCI at -0.55 and still easing, HY OAS at 2.79% (32nd percentile), supporting risk assets and a mild equity upside drift.
Fed balance sheet is growing slowly via reserve management bill purchases; repo traded below IORB in May and reserves are ample, so there is no funding-stress catalyst for spread widening near term.

The tightening impulse is coming through rates instead: 2y and 10y are at 1-year highs (99th percentile) after +55bp/+38bp in 3 months, with a hawkish-leaning FOMC on July 29. This leaves yields stretched, but with momentum, so the edge for mean reversion is only slight.
Dollar spec longs are at the 99th percentile, and the 1-month dollar trend has turned lower, so crowded positioning tilts the dollar slightly downward over 3 months.
HY spreads are very tight while borrowing costs rise and private credit outflows build, so the spread risk is skewed modestly wider at the 3-month horizon, though carry dominates near term.
VIX at 18.6 is above its median with conditions loose, implying mild downward drift absent a funding shock; the oil spike (+28% in 1 month) is prone to partial retracement.

10y yields sit at the 99th percentile of their 1y range while speculative TY positioning is deeply short (18th percentile, adding 48k last week): a crowded short that leaves room for a squeeze lower in yields, though momentum and the July 29 FOMC keep the edge modest.
Spec DX longs are at the 99th percentile of the 52-week range, a crowded dollar long that tilts the dollar lower on 1m–3m horizons.

ES spec positioning is near flat but at a 52-week high and rising; with the VIX at a moderate 18.6, HY spreads tight but not extreme, and the NFCI loose, the risk appetite backdrop favors the usual positive equity drift.

VIX spec shorts are less crowded than usual (39th percentile), so short-vol unwind risk is limited; a VIX slightly above its long-run median, with event risk passing after the FOMC, implies a mild bias lower.
Oil has rallied 28% in a month but spec longs are only at the 36th percentile, so positioning is not stretched; after the spike, mean reversion slightly dominates at longer horizons.
Gold sits at the 5th percentile of its 1y range after a 15% 3m drop, with spec length moderate (43rd percentile); washed-out sentiment gives a small upside tilt.

Foreign central banks (ECB hiking, UK pricing further hikes) are hawkish into an energy shock, limiting how far US-foreign rate differentials can widen; global yields rising alongside US caps the case for a US-specific yield reversal near term.

The oil re-spike (+28% in a month) hurts energy-importing Europe and Asia more than the US net energy exporter, a terms-of-trade tailwind for the dollar, but DX speculative longs at the 99th percentile make further dollar upside crowded.

US 2y and 10y yields sit at 1-year highs with the Fed's easing bias removed; the July 29 FOMC is a hawkish-tilt risk for the front end, but over 3 months, if oil supply disruptions ease, mild mean reversion and some re-steepening are slightly favored.
Gold near its 1-year low reflects a strong dollar and high real yields; there is no clear global catalyst either way, so it is held neutral.
Strong AI-driven earnings abroad and in the US, plus easy financial conditions (NFCI -0.55), keep the equity drift positive. A stretched oil move favors some mean reversion in crude and breakevens.

WTI rebounded 28.5% in a month to $91.74 after the June US-Iran MOU had pushed it lower, signaling renewed Hormuz/supply risk. After such a sharp move, and with a likely backwardated curve implying lower spot drift, I lean modestly toward mean reversion over 1-3 months.
Speculative crude length is only at the 36th percentile but rising, so positioning is not stretched. That argues against a sharp near-term collapse in oil.

The oil rebound feeds headline inflation and the hawkish Fed narrative: many participants see the funds rate above the current range by year-end, and the FOMC meets July 29. This gives a slight upward bias to 2y/10y yields and bear-flattening near term.
10y breakevens rose only 8bp against a 28% oil rally. Breakevens likely catch up near term, but fade if oil retraces over 3 months.

The US as a net energy exporter, plus wider rate differentials, gives mild dollar support. Gold sits at its 5th percentile after a 15% drop as real yields rose, so I see roughly balanced odds with slight rebound potential.

Higher energy prices support HY energy issuers, keeping spreads tight near term, while the energy cost drag on consumers is a modest headwind for equities. The equity drift stays positive given AI-driven earnings.

WTI +28.5% in a month and +10% last week signals the June US-Iran MOU / Hormuz reopening optimism is fraying; geopolitical premium rebuilt, but two-way headline risk and eventual de-escalation skew 3m oil modestly lower.
Gold near its 1y low despite active Middle East conflict; geopolitical hedging demand plus depressed level argue slight upside bias.

Rates already at 1y highs on an oil/inflation-driven hawkish Fed repricing; a geopolitical resolution would pull short-end and breakevens lower, while escalation is partly priced — slight downside skew at 3m.

Equities have absorbed conflict shocks on AI earnings strength; HY spreads tight and VIX mid-range, leaving room for modest vol/spread widening into pre-midterm (Nov 2026) campaign season and tariff noise.
Dollar balanced: safe-haven bid on escalation offset by rate-differential sensitivity if Fed hawkishness fades.

thesis: Yields sit at 1-year highs. A hawkish Fed has dropped its easing bias, a few members float hikes, and the oil re-spike feeds inflation fears, so near-term momentum and the July 29 FOMC keep rates roughly balanced. Over 3 months, crowded TY and TU shorts, extended levels and possible geopolitical easing tilt 2y and 10y slightly lower. The curve leans toward mild re-steepening, helped by coupon supply against an anchored bill supply. Equities keep their positive drift on AI earnings, loose financial conditions (NFCI -0.55) and a firm labor market with claims at 187k. VIX drifts slightly lower from an above-median level once event risk passes. Oil's 28% one-month spike is prone to partial mean reversion, though spec length isn't stretched, so the near term is close to neutral. Gold is washed out at its 5th percentile and gets a small rebound tilt despite high real yields. The dollar is neutral, with rate-differential support offset by crowded DX longs. HY spreads are tight and carry dominates near term, with mild widening risk at 3 months as private credit outflows and higher borrowing costs build. Breakevens get a slight near-term catch-up to oil that fades if crude retraces.
